## Verdict: REJECT (one Important checklist failure: the release note overstates what stayed unchanged)

The PR is not ready to merge: its release-note fragment says tool and resource error messages are unchanged, but errors the 2.x SDK raises outside a tool's function keep the SDK's own text.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

- VC-2: FAIL (important) — The release note states tools, widget resources, tool and resource error messages, and stdio and Streamable HTTP endpoints are unchanged by the mcp 2.x migration. [changelog.d/391.changed.md:1]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  changelog.d/391.changed.md:1 says 'Tools, widget resources, tool and resource error messages, and the stdio and Streamable HTTP endpoints are unchanged.' Head server.py does preserve 1.x text only for exceptions raised inside the tool/resource function: _tool_errors (server.py:204-227) converts Exception to ToolError(str(exc)) and _resource_errors (230-250) to ResourceError('Error reading resource <uri>: <exc>'); both are applied via the _tool/_resource helpers (338-348). But criterion 15 (criteria.json) states errors 2.x raises outside the tool's function (argument validation, output conversion) keep the 2.x SDK's own text, and that the JSON-RPC error code of a failed resource read is now set by the 2.x SDK; server.py cannot wrap those (they occur outside the wrapped fn). So the unqualified 'error messages ... unchanged' is overbroad: a client sending invalid arguments to a tool gets SDK-produced text, not the 1.x text. Also the PR itself adds client-visible changes in the same note (max_sse_event_size for widget reads, serverInfo key on results per criterion 15). I did not read mcp SDK source (no dependency_sources), so the exact 1.x vs 2.x validation text is taken from criterion 15 and the _tool_errors docstring, not independently diffed. Tool/resource registrations (query_results_widget, tools) and the /mcp endpoint wiring are otherwise unchanged apart from the FastMCP->MCPServer rename.

  </details>
